action: Run redo across three operation types in the local sandbox, reading the per-symbol drawing store at every step
response: CASE A (property edit, prior pass): Set level to 755.25 → Undo restored the sloped endpoints → Redo did NOT re-apply 755.25, while reporting disabled=false. CASE B (placement, immediately after a page load, run TWICE): place → count 2→3 → Undo → 3→2 → Redo BUTTON STAYED DISABLED and clicking it changed nothing. CASE C (placement, later in a longer session): count 2 → Undo → 1 → Redo ENABLED → Redo → back to 2. Redo genuinely worked.
result: ⭐ REDO IS INCONSISTENT, NOT UNIFORMLY BROKEN — it works in a warm session and fails on the first undo after a page load
url: self-measured, local sandbox 127.0.0.1:8091, 390x844 frame, 2026-09-07; case B reproduced twice from a fresh reload
notes: ⭐ THIS SUPERSEDES BOTH EARLIER REDO ROWS AND CORRECTS MY OWN OVERSTATEMENT. UCT-UNDO-0002 concluded 'Redo does not cover property edits'; the fuller picture is worse in one way and better in another. BETTER: redo is NOT dead — case C restored a placement correctly, so the feature is real and TradingView still has no redo at all on mobile. WORSE: the failure is in the FIRST-USE path, which is the one a real user meets — open the chart, draw something, undo it, and Redo is greyed out with the action unrecoverable. Also note a related and separately verified fact: after a page reload BOTH Undo and Redo are disabled while the DRAWINGS persist, so the history does not survive a reload even though the objects do. ⛔ VERDICT ON THE UCT_AHEAD: keep it, but qualified. UCT shipping Undo+Redo in the drawing bar is still ahead of TradingView shipping neither redo nor a second arrow — but the claim must be written as 'Redo exists and works within a session; it does not arm on the first undo after load', never as a clean win.

target: Why the real-device pass did not run
action: Start an iPhone 15 / iOS 17.5 App Live session, open Safari, and load the tunnelled sandbox
response: Safari returned BrowserStack's own error page: 'Unable to connect to the page you requested. Trying to test a private URL or localhost? Click on Local Testing in the toolbar and follow the instructions to enable Local Testing!' — for both http://bs-local.com:8091/charts and http://localhost:8091/charts. The session's Local Testing panel offered only 'Download Local Desktop App', with no connected state and no field for a local identifier.
result: ⛔ BLOCKED — the tunnel is healthy but namespaced, and App Live cannot request a namespaced tunnel
url: self-measured 2026-09-07; tunnel process inspected on the host
notes: ⛔ DIAGNOSED, NOT GUESSED. Host-side evidence: two BrowserStackLocal processes running since 19:26, the child holding THIRTY established TLS connections to BrowserStack IPs on 443 — so the tunnel is genuinely up and authenticated. Command-line inspection (flag presence only; the key was never read or printed) shows BOTH processes carry '--local-identifier uctp1'. A tunnel started with a local identifier is NAMESPACED: only sessions that explicitly request that identifier may use it. App Live is manual/UI-driven and exposes no capability layer, so it can only bind to the account's DEFAULT, identifier-less tunnel — which is why the device sees no tunnel at all. Independently confirmed that the sandbox itself is fine: curl to http://bs-local.com:8091/charts from the host returned 200. ⭐ ONE-LINE FIX: restart the tunnel WITHOUT the identifier — BrowserStackLocal.exe --key <KEY> — or run a second identifier-less tunnel alongside it. Nothing else about the setup needs to change.
